goal: Apply `transcript` graders (`max_turns`, `max_total_tokens`, `max_wall_seconds`) as hard limits that abort a runaway run and as graders at validation time, persisting each evaluation to `grader_results` with the documented observed-vs-breached payload.

constraints: Hard-limit enforcement and validation-time grading share the same `transcript` spec on the task — there is one source of truth, not two parallel configs.
Hard limits abort the run when breached: `max_turns` halts the agent before the grader stage is reached (per `docs/loop.md`); `max_total_tokens` and `max_wall_seconds` do the same.

Validation-time grading produces a `grader_results` row whose `payload_json` matches the documented transcript shape: `{observed: {turns, total_tokens, wall_seconds}, breached: "max_turns" | "max_total_tokens" | "max_wall_seconds"}`.
Run-cost-order is respected: transcript graders run after command graders pass; a transcript failure aborts later (more expensive) types per `docs/task-schema.md`.
At least one of `max_turns`, `max_total_tokens`, `max_wall_seconds` must be set on a transcript grader; absent that, the grader is rejected at task-validation time, not at run time.
non_goals: Re-implementing token accounting — token counts come from the invoker's SDK signals.
edge_cases: Multiple transcript fields set on one grader (e.g. both `max_turns` and `max_wall_seconds`) — the first-breached field is the one recorded in `breached`.
A run that completes within all limits still produces a passing `grader_results` row recording the observed values.
Wall-clock measurement must be monotonic — system clock changes during a run must not flip the verdict.
Token totals come from `ResultMessage` / cumulative SDK accounting; the runner must not double-count thinking vs output tokens.
A run aborted by hard-limit enforcement still records the transcript grader as failed at validation time — the abort and the grading row agree on the breached field.

assertions: Transcript constraints are enforced as hard limits during a run (aborting before further turns) AND as graders at validation time, both reading the same `transcript` spec on the task.
Each validation-time evaluation writes a `grader_results` row whose `payload_json` matches the documented transcript shape (`observed: {turns, total_tokens, wall_seconds}`, `breached: ...`).
Run-cost-order is preserved: transcript graders only run after command graders pass, and a transcript breach skips later (rubric/manual) types.
Tests cover passing runs and breaches of each of the three limit fields, demonstrating that a hard-limit abort and the persisted grader row agree on the breached field.
graders.name: transcript-grader-contract
